schema: Psalm gloss overrides (Benedictine psalter, Vulgate Gallican). Keyed by the exact lexicon key (lowercase printed form). Each value is an `edited` card the reader shows on click: { lemma?, pos?, gloss, note? }. Where `lemma`/`pos` are omitted the entry keeps Whitaker's. The note gives the psalm of first occurrence (Psalm = Hebrew numbering, matching `latin.md`) plus a familiar verse. This is a STARTER set — refine glosses and confirm verse citations before shipping.

misericordia.gloss: mercy — God's steadfast covenant love (Heb. ḥesed), the psalter's great theme.
misericordia.note: First occurs Ps 6: 'miserere mei, Domine'. The constant refrain 'misericordia tua in aeternum' — God's loyal love endures forever (e.g. Pss 102, 117).

misericordiae.gloss: of mercy — of steadfast covenant love.
misericordiae.note: 'In multitudine misericordiae tuae' (Ps 5), the plea for the abundance of God's mercy; 'memorare misericordiae tuae' (Ps 24).

misericordiam.gloss: mercy (acc.) — the loving-kindness asked of God.
misericordiam.note: First Ps 5: 'in multitudine misericordiae tuae introlbo in domum tuam'. Israel begs it ('fac nobiscum misericordiam') throughout.

misericordias.gloss: mercies — God's multiple deeds of steadfast love.
misericordias.note: Ps 7 ends 'et cantabo... misericordias Domini'; the plural gathers God's many saving acts into remembered song.

miserationes.gloss: compassions, tender mercies — the pity of God toward the weak.
miserationes.note: First Ps 12: 'propter miserationes...' — closer to 'pity' than 'mercy', of God's readiness to bend toward the lowly.

miserere.gloss: have mercy (on) — the imperative opening Israel's great cry.
miserere.note: 'Miserere mei, Deus' (Ps 50/51) and 'miserere nostri' (Pss 4, 6, 9...) — the psalm's most repeated plea; David's repentance psalm (50).

misericors.gloss: merciful, compassionate — an attribute of God.
misericors.note: God is 'misericors et miserator' (Pss 102, 110) — merciful and compassionate, slow to anger.

iustitia.gloss: righteousness, justice — God's saving order, not mere retribution.
iustitia.note: First Ps 9: 'iudicabit orbem terrae in iustitia'. In the psalter God's 'iustitia' is salvation breaking in (Pss 7, 35, 88).

iustitiae.note: Ps 2: 'iustitias Domini' — recounting the righteous deeds of the Lord in song.

iustitiam.note: First Ps 9: 'in iustitia tua' — pleads to be led 'in God's righteousness', for vindication and deliverance.

iustus.gloss: righteous (one) — the just man, upright and God-fearing.
iustus.note: First Ps 12: 'beati qui... iusti'; 'Dominus iustus' (Ps 10); the righteous flourish 'sicut palma' (Ps 91).

iniquitas.gloss: iniquity, guilt — injustice and wrong that separates from God.
iniquitas.note: First Ps 4: 'usquequo... diligitis vanitatem, et quaeritis mendacium' pairs iniquity's fruit with vanity. God does not impute it where there is forgiveness (Ps 31).

iniquitatis.note: First Ps 5: 'virum sanguinum et dolosum abominabitur Dominus' — the way of iniquity's children.

iniquitatem.note: First Ps 5: 'propter... iniquitatem odisti'. David's 'delictum meum cognitum tibi feci, et iniquitatem meam non abscondi' (Ps 31).

iniquitates.note: First Ps 10: 'multiplicatae sunt iniquitates' — the many sins that 'prolapsed' the psalmist to mercy.

iniquus.gloss: unjust, iniquitous — the wicked opposed to the righteous.
iniquus.note: Ps 23/24: 'quis ascendet in montem Domini? innocens manibus et mundo corde' — the just are set against the iniquus.

vanitas.gloss: vanity — breath, vapor (Heb. hēbel); all that is fleeting and empty.
vanitas.note: First Ps 6 (printed 'uanitas'); 'universa vanitas omnis homo vivens' (Ps 38) — every living one is vanity. 'Vanitas vanitatum' is Ecclesiastes, but the psalmist applies 'hēbel' to human life founded on self.

vanitatem.gloss: vanity (acc.) — empty, fleeting things chased by the foolish.
vanitatem.note: First Ps 3: 'ut quid diligitis vanitatem, et quaeritis mendacium' (Ps 4) — why love what is vain and seek a lie?

vanitates.gloss: vanities — empty follies and false idols.
vanitates.note: First Ps 7: 'nemo... qui sequitur vanitates' (Ps 30) — false gods and empty pursuits are vanitates that miss God's mercy.

desiderium.gloss: desire, longing — the reaching of the soul toward God.
desiderium.note: First Ps 38: 'desiderium animae tuae... tribues eis' — God grants the heart's desire granted to those who wait (Pss 20, 37).

desideria.gloss: desires — inclinations of the heart, for good or ill.
desideria.note: First Ps 13: 'Dominus... desideria pauperum exaudivit' — God hears the desires of the poor.

salus.gloss: salvation, deliverance, safety — God's rescue and health.
salus.note: First Ps 3: 'Domine, salus mea' — the psalter's constant hope; 'in Deo salutare vultus mei' (Pss 41, 42).

salutis.note: First Ps 3: 'Deus salutis meae' — the God of my salvation, answering from his holy hill (Ps 3:9).

salutem.note: First Ps 17: 'proclamavi... salutem' (Ps 17/18) — David, saved, lifts 'the cup of salvation' (Ps 115).

veritas.gloss: truth, faithfulness — God's constancy (Heb. 'emeth), paired with mercy.
veritas.note: First Ps 10: 'misericordia et veritas' — mercy and truth together (Pss 24, 56, 88); God's word is truth (Ps 118/119).

confessio.gloss: praise, thanksgiving — in the psalter chiefly of God, NOT guilt-confession.
confessio.note: First Ps 6: 'confitebimur tibi Deus' — 'confessio' here means giving God thanks/praise. A key psalter usage to set apart from modern 'confession'.

confessionem.gloss: praise, thanksgiving (acc.) — an offering of thanks.
confessionem.note: Ps 1: 'in laetitia' / 'vox exultationis et salutis in tabernaculis iustorum' (Ps 117) frames confessio as joyful public thanks.

confessionis.note: First Ps 5: 'introibo in domum tuam in multitudine misericordiae tuae' — worship entered with confession of praise.

confitebor.gloss: I will give thanks / I praise — psalter sense of 'ἐξομολογοῦμαι'.
confitebor.note: 'Confitebor tibi' opens many songs (Pss 9, 30, 41, 108...): the singer proclaims God's praise publicly.

confitemini.gloss: give thanks, praise — the repeated imperative of the hallels.
confitemini.note: 'Confitemini Domino quoniam bonus' (Pss 105, 106, 117, 135) — 'give thanks to the Lord, for he is good'.

gloria.gloss: glory — God's splendor and honor, reflected on the righteous.
gloria.note: First Ps 4: 'et gloria mea... exalta caput meum'; Ps 8: 'quam admirabile est nomen tuum... super omnem gloriam'.

gloriam.note: First Ps 6: 'ut cantem gloriam tuam' — singing God's glory; 'da gloriam Deo' (Ps 67).

gloriae.note: First Ps 7: 'rex gloriae' (Ps 23/24) — 'the Lord strong and mighty, the King of glory' at the gates.

laudate.note: 'Laudate Dominum' opens and closes the final hallel (Pss 145-150); Ps 148-150 call all creation to praise.

laudatio.gloss: praise — the act/utterance of praising God.
laudatio.note: Ps 9: 'pro admirabilibus tuis laudabo te' (Ps 9:2); Psalm titles use it of the song itself.

alleluia.gloss: Hallelujah — 'praise Yah' (Heb. halelu-yah), untranslated shout of praise.
alleluia.note: Vulgate keeps the Hebrew 'alleluia' in psalm titles and the closing hallels (Pss 104-106, 110-118, 134-150).

psalterium.gloss: psaltery — a plucked stringed instrument; also 'the psalter' as the book.
psalterium.note: Ps 150: 'laudate eum in psalterio et cithara' — with psaltery and harp; the psalter's own title-name.

psalterio.note: Ps 2: 'psallite Deo in cithara, in psalterio et voce psalmi' (Pss 32, 70) — worship with strings.

cithara.gloss: harp, lyre — the instrument of psalm-song.
cithara.note: Pairs with psalterium (Pss 32, 70, 107, 150); 'surgam diluculo, quia cithara tibi, Deus' (Ps 56).

peccatum.gloss: sin — the offense against God confessed for forgiveness.
peccatum.note: First Ps 36: 'peccatum meum cognitum tibi feci' (Ps 31) — the confessed sin is not imputed by God; the faithful who confide in the Lord do not stumble.

peccata.note: Ps 1: 'in tota lege Domini voluntas eius' contrasted with the 'via peccatorum' the blessed do not walk.

peccator.gloss: sinner — the ungodly, set against the righteous.
peccator.note: First Ps 17: 'misit de excelso et accepit me' — David delivered from the hand of the peccator; 'peccatores peribunt' (Ps 36).

spes.gloss: hope — confident expectation in God's deliverance.
spes.note: First Ps 6: 'spes mea in Deo'; Ps 38: 'quae est expectatio mea? nonne Dominus?' — my hope is in the Lord.

timor.gloss: fear — reverent awe of the Lord, beginning of wisdom.
timor.note: First Ps 3: 'in timore tuo' (Ps 5); 'initium sapientiae timor Domini' (Ps 110/111); the blessed fear the Lord (Ps 1, 111).

timore.note: First Ps 11: 'servite Domino in timore' (Ps 2:11) — serve the Lord with fear and rejoice with trembling.

timorem.gloss: fear (acc.) — the holy awe of God.
timorem.note: Ps 12: 'domine... imple timore' — 'the fear of the Lord is clean, enduring forever' (Ps 18/19).

bonitate.gloss: goodness of God — his benevolence, the ground of thanks.
bonitate.note: 'Confitemini Domino quoniam bonus... quoniam in aeternum misericordia eius' (Pss 105-106, 117) — because he is good, his mercy endures forever.

bonitatem.gloss: goodness (acc.) — God's kindness tasted and proclaimed.
bonitatem.note: First Ps 7: 'gustate et videte quoniam suavis est Dominus' (Ps 33) — taste that the Lord is good.

benignitatem.gloss: kindness (acc.), graciousness — mild favor near to mercy.
benignitatem.note: First Ps 5: 'miserere mei' answered by 'in multitudine misericordiae tuae'; God's benignitas is his gentle goodness (Ps 30).

benignitatis.note: First Ps 12: recalled with mercy — 'quoniam in aeternum misericordia eius' (Ps 117) shows the constancy behind God's benignitas.

exsultatio.gloss: rejoicing, exultation — the gladness of the delivered.
exsultatio.note: First Ps 7: 'voces exultationis et salutis in tabernaculis iustorum' (Ps 117) — sounds of joy and salvation in the tents of the righteous.

iubilate.gloss: shout for joy (imperative pl.) — jubilant, wordless praise.
iubilate.note: 'Iubilate Deo omnis terra' (Pss 65, 97/100) — make a joyful noise to the Lord, all the earth. The Gallican uses v-/u- plainly.

exsultate.gloss: rejoice, exult (imperative pl.) — burst into glad song.
exsultate.note: First Ps 11: 'exsultate, iusti, in Domino' (Ps 32) — rejoice in the Lord, you righteous; the deliverance song of the just.
